what: Watsco distributes air conditioning and heating equipment. It buys from Carrier, Rheem and others and sells through about 700 branches to the contractors who install and repair systems.
customers: Heating and air conditioning contractors across the United States, Canada, Mexico and Latin America.
money: air conditioners, furnaces and heat pumps
moat: Branches near contractors who need a part the same morning, in a business where the distributor who has it in stock gets the sale. The network is the moat.
risks: Replacement demand depends on weather and on consumers' willingness to spend
Revenue fell from $7.6B to $7.2B last year as a refrigerant transition disrupted buying
26 times earnings for a distributor with a 6.9% net margin
opportunities: $666M of free cash flow and $733M of cash against $942M of debt
Analysts see about 18% upside, and the dividend has been raised for decades
Most of the market is still served by small independent distributors, which Watsco keeps buying
watch: Same-branch sales growth and equipment unit volumes separate from price.
